chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated, saying: Al-Qassim ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Hazim narrated, saying: 'Ubays ibn Hisham an-Nashiri narrated from Abdullah ibn Jibilla, from al-Hakam ibn Ayman, from Ward (the brother of al-Kumayt), from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him) that he said:

Indeed, before the appearance of this Command (al-Qa'im), the moon will be eclipsed for five days remaining, and the sun for fifteen days, and that will be in the month of Ramadan, and at that time the calculations of the astrologers will fail.

key_terms.بين يدي هذا الأمر: Before the appearance of this Command (al-Qa'im)
key_terms.لِخَمْسٍ تَبْقَى: For five days remaining (of the month)

ai.seo_question: What celestial signs precede the appearance of the Mahdi according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the precise timing of the Mahdi’s appearance, linking the celestial phenomena of lunar and solar eclipses to the month of Ramadan, a period of heightened spiritual significance in Shia eschatology. The failure of astrologers' calculations (*hisab*) underscores the transition from human predictive science to divine decree, affirming that the Mahdi’s advent is a unique, divinely orchestrated event that transcends natural laws.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (46) Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Sa’eed narrated from al-Qassim bin Muhammad bin al-Hasan bin Hazim from Obayss bin Hisham an-Nashiri from Abdullah bin Jibilla from al-Hakam bin Ayman from Ward, al-Kumayt’s brother, that Abu Ja’far al-Baqir (as) had said:

“Before the appearance of al-Qa’im, the moon will be eclipsed five days before the end of the month and the sun will be eclipsed in the middle of the month. That will occur in Ramadan and then the calculations of the astrologers will fail.”
